newsitem.title: USA: KCBT says wheat futures volume likely set record.
newsitem.headline: KCBT says wheat futures volume likely set record.

text.p: Trading volume in Kansas City Board of Trade hard red winter wheat futures on Monday likely set a new single-day record for the contract because of a surge in harvest-related activity, the KCBT said in a statement.

Trading volume in KCBT wheat was estimated at 81.35 million bushels, well above the previous single-day record of 79.055 million bushels set April 11. Official volume figures for Monday's trade will be released Tuesday morning.
Increased harvest activity in U.S. HRW growing areas contributed in large part to the futures volume, traders said.
Harvest reports Kansas, the top-producing HRW wheat state, indicated that both crop yields and quality were better than previously expected, particularly after a freeze hit some areas in April.
"Trading activity is expected to remain brisk in coming days as harvest continues to move north," the KCBT said.
